results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Pull-Up
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to an overhead position. Stand underneath the handles and grasp them with an overhand grip (palms facing forward), shoulder-width apart. Bend and cross your legs for stability.
Engage your back and pull yourself up by bending your elbows and driving them down and back, lifting your chest towards the handles.
Continue pulling until your chest is close to the handles, and slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core tight to maintain stability and prevent your body from swinging.
Start with fewer repetitions and gradually increase as your strength improves.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull yourself up and inhale as you lower yourself down.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Pull-Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Core.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Wide Grip Inverted Row on Floor
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about waist height. Stand facing the handles, holding the handles with an overhand grip (palms facing down) just wider than shoulder width. Lean back with your body straight, heels on the floor, and arms extended.
Engage your back and pull your chest towards the handles by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue pulling until your chest is close to the handles and your elbows are almost fully bent.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull your chest towards the handles and inhale as you extend your arms back.
Focus on using your back muscles to perform the row, avoiding excessive use of your arms.
Adjust the angle of your body to increase or decrease the difficulty of the exercise.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Wide Grip Inverted Row on Floor is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

results.name: Theraband Scapula Retraction
instructions: Hold a resistance band in front of you at chest height with both hands, arms straight.
Stand or sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, pulling the band slightly apart without bending your elbows.
Release slowly to the start and repeat.
tips: The movement is small and comes only from your shoulder blades.
Don't shrug your shoulders toward your ears.
results.description: Theraband Scapula Retraction is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Rear Shoulders, Traps.

results.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
instructions: Stand in the center of a trap bar with your feet shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees and hips to lower your body, and grasp the trap bar handles with a neutral grip (palms facing in).
Engage your core; keep your chest up and your back straight. Push through your heels to lift the trap bar off the floor, extending your hips and knees simultaneously.
Stand up straight, pulling your shoulders back at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the bar back to the floor by bending your hips and knees, maintaining a straight back. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your chest remains up and your back stays straight to avoid injury.
Push through your heels to engage your glutes and hamstrings effectively.
Avoid locking your knees completely at the top of the movement to maintain tension in your muscles.
results.description: Trap Bar Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a trap bar, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Traps, Forearms.

results.name: V Bar Lat Pull Down
instructions: Sit at a lat pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads. Grasp the V-bar attached to the machine, arms fully extended above you, and hands shoulder-width apart.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest and bring your elbows downwards.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return the V-bar to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on using your back muscles to pull the bar, avoiding excessive use of your arms.
Keep your wrists straight and avoid bending them during the pull to prevent strain.
results.description: V Bar Lat Pull Down is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Weighted Back Extensions on Hyperextension Bench
instructions: Set the pad of the hyperextension bench just below your hips and hook your heels under the foot pads.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Lower your torso by hinging at the hips until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Raise your torso until your body forms a straight line, squeezing your glutes, and repeat.
tips: Don't hyperextend your lower back at the top.
Keep the weight tight to your chest.
results.description: Weighted Back Extensions on Hyperextension Bench is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

results.name: Alternate Biceps Curl Resistance Band
instructions: Stand on the center of the resistance band with your feet shoulder width apart and hold one handle in each hand, palms facing each other (neutral grip).
Supinate your grip as you curl your right arm toward your shoulder, while the opposite arm remains extended.
Lower the resistance band handle slowly to the starting position and immediately curl up your left arm, repeating the same motion.
Continue alternating arms while maintaining an upright posture and steady tempo.
tips: Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso throughout the exercise.
Avoid swinging your body or using momentum to lift the band.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of each curl before lowering and lower the band slowly to maximize muscle engagement.
Exhale as you curl the band upward and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Alternate Biceps Curl Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Forearms, Shoulders.

results.name: Alternate Biceps Curl Standing Dumbbells
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended by your sides. Your palms should face forward (supinated grip).
Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your torso. Slowly curl the right dumbbell up towards your shoulder, maintaining the forward-facing position of your palms.
Squeeze your bicep at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the same motion with your left arm, alternating between right and left arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your elbows stay close to your torso and avoid swinging your arms to lift the weights.
Move your arms slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Focus on fully extending your arms at the bottom of each curl to engage the full range of motion.
results.description: Alternate Biceps Curl Standing Dumbbells is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Alternate Hammer Curl Seated Dumbbells
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended by your sides. Your palms should face each other (neutral grip).
Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your torso. Slowly curl the right dumbbell up towards your shoulder, maintaining the neutral grip with your palm facing inward.
Squeeze your bicep at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the same motion with your left arm, alternating between right and left arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your wrists straight to avoid putting unnecessary strain on them during the curls.
Maintain a controlled pace to ensure that you're using muscle strength rather than momentum.
Visualize the bicep contraction to enhance the mind-muscle connection for better results.
results.description: Alternate Hammer Curl Seated Dumbbells is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Alternate Hammer Curl Standing Dumbbells
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended by your sides. Your palms should face each other (neutral grip).
Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your torso. Slowly curl the right dumbbell up towards your shoulder, maintaining the neutral grip with your palm facing inward.
Squeeze your bicep at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the same motion with your left arm, alternating between right and left arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your wrists straight to avoid putting unnecessary strain on them during the curls.
Maintain a controlled pace to ensure that you're using muscle strength rather than momentum.
Keep your back straight and shoulders back to maintain proper posture.
results.description: Alternate Hammer Curl Standing Dumbbells is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.
